findings.reason: Operations.js:307 defines `__iterator` as an arrow function, so `this` comes from `reverseFactory`. Every caller (CollectionImpl.js:259 and 573, Operations.js:61) calls `reverseFactory` as a plain function inside an ES module, so `this` is undefined. Line 320 now reads `this.size` when reverse=true and useKeys=false. That means `Seq([1,2,3]).reverse().map(x=>x).reverse().values().next()` throws. The diff removed the `reversedSequence.size` reference that avoided this.
findings.claim: Reverse iteration of a reversed indexed sequence throws TypeError because `this.size` is read inside the arrow function `reversedSequence.__iterator`, where `this` is undefined.
findings.evidence: The diff swaps `reversedSequence.size - ++i` for `this.size - ++i` and deletes the comment that explained why: "`__iterator` is an arrow function, so `this` is not the reversed sequence here — read `reversedSequence.size` explicitly." At line 307, `reversedSequence.__iterator = (type, reverse) => {...}` is an arrow function, and so is the callback passed to `new Iterator`. Both take `this` lexically from `reverseFactory`. Every caller invokes `reverseFactory` as a plain function: `reverseFactory(this, false)` at CollectionImpl.js:573, `reverseFactory(this, true)` at CollectionImpl.js:259 and Operations.js:61. In this strict-mode ES module that makes `this` undefined. Trigger: `Seq([1,2,3]).reverse().map(x => x).reverse().values().next()`. The outer reversed sequence's `__iterator(type, false)` calls `mapped.__iterator(ITERATE_ENTRIES, true)`, which calls the inner `reversedSequence.__iterator(…, true)`. With `useKeys` false and `reverse` true, that evaluates `this.size` and throws "Cannot read properties of undefined". By contrast, `__iterate` at line 298 is a `function` expression, so `this.size` at line 303 works there; the `__iterator` path is different. No test in the repo exercises this reverse-iterator path, which is how the change passes the suite.
